why: In a double-quoted PowerShell string a backtick is the escape character, so a commit message typed as -m "use `actions/checkout`" stores BEL where the Markdown code span began; a real history carries three of them, and a published commit cannot be reworded. A bell, vertical tab or form feed rings or moves the cursor and hides no text, so in a commit message it is a note. A backspace overwrites what the terminal printed, so it still fails. The pass side has one commit with the PowerShell shape (BEL before the letters of two code spans); the fail side has one commit with a backspace. Whoever fails every C0 control in a message turns the pass side red; whoever lets every control in a message through turns the fail side green. Messages are base64 because rebar reads its own caso.json raw.
